note: A contradiction the F02 text fix introduced, found by screenshotting the board afterwards. The value was corrected; the swatch beside it was not.

rows.why: F02 · THE SWATCH STILL SAID BLUE. zz-f02-resolved corrected the Fill VALUE to #F3F4F6 — the hero's measured paint — but a text row cannot touch the colour chip beside it, so the panel then contradicted itself in a new way: the readout said #F3F4F6 while the 28x28 chip stayed #1A56DB. That is the same defect F02 reported, just moved one node to the left, and only the screenshot showed it. Read first rather than inferred: the Fill row is 52:126, its control 52:128, and the control's three children are the swatch 52:129 (28x28, #1A56DB), the input 52:130 holding the hex text, and the binding chip 52:132. op:fill compares before writing and reports SAME if it already matches, so it is idempotent.

F02 · the same swatch on the second board. Its id was READ, not inferred from the sibling pattern — control 199:374's children are 199:375 (swatch, #1A56DB), 199:376 (input) and 199:378 (binding chip). Guessing 199:375 from 52:129's position would have been right here, but a wrong guess paints an unrelated node grey and fill has no expect guard, so the read was worth its call.
